basics.name: RoyMech (Roy Beardmore's mechanical engineering reference site)
basics.url: https://roymech.org/ (the archived re-release that was opened; resources index https://roymech.org/Useful_Tables/index.html). The original domain www.roymech.co.uk showed up in search results but returned a SiteGround captcha page and could not be opened from this environment [uncertain]
basics.resource_type: encyclopedia/wiki (single-author engineering reference website of notes, tables and formulae; not openly editable)
basics.license: All rights reserved: roymech.org's Notes page reads 'Copyright (c) 2000 - Roy Beardmore, All Rights Reserved' and the site footer reads '(c) 2020 Roymech.org', with a disclaimer that the information is for general purposes only. No open licence, so link to pages but do not copy text or diagrams
basics.language: English (British engineering usage and BS/ISO/DIN standards)
basics.year: First issued 2 September 2000 (Notes page); Roy Beardmore's own last update noted as 18 December 2009; he died on 9 March 2013. roymech.org re-released the saved content verbatim (footer (c) 2020; its sitemap shows 580 URLs with the original 2001 lastmod dates). According to search-result snippets, roymech.co.uk was restored to active publication by Andrew Wade with a new menu system [uncertain]
basics.access_barrier: none for roymech.org; roymech.co.uk sits behind a bot-check (captcha) page that ordinary browsers pass automatically [uncertain]
basics.image_license: Same as text: all rights reserved. Diagrams are small GIF line drawings (e.g. /images/Coupling_rigid.gif, /images/mechanism_24.gif); some drawings appear to be adapted from textbooks and suppliers' catalogues [uncertain]
basics.authority_level: educator (a practising UK mechanical engineer's personal reference notes, drawing on British Standards and textbooks such as Uicker, Pennock and Shigley's Theory of Machines and Mechanisms; not peer-reviewed; well known and recommended on engineering forums)

coverage.covers: Broad mechanical-engineering reference: Drive Components (38 pages: rigid, muff, beam, pin, rubber-disc, spider (jaw), Bibby, chain, gear, diaphragm (MetaFlex), fluid and universal couplings; plate, cone, eddy-current, dog, fluid and sprag clutches; band, block, disc and drum brakes and friction materials; spur, helical, bevel, worm, epicyclic and harmonic gears, gearboxes and differentials; belts, timing belts, V-belts, roller chain; bearings, shafts, seals, drive motors), Machine Elements (cams, escapements, flywheels, indexing mechanisms, ratchets, reciprocating and rocking mechanisms, power screws, shock absorbers, plus a 'Mechanisms' page), Springs (helical compression/extension/torsion, disc, leaf, spiral), Keyways and splines, Circlips and pins, Screws and fastenings (including a 'Screw Locking and Retaining Methods' page), Rivets, Welds, Adhesives (natural, rubber/contact, thermoplastic incl. PVA and cyanoacrylate, thermoset incl. epoxy, anaerobic, toughened), plus materials, tolerances and fits, tribology, fatigue, lifting, seals, pumps, valves and more. About 580 pages in the roymech.org sitemap
coverage.organisation: Hierarchical menus by engineering subject (Background, Engineering, Design, Components 1 and 2), each leading to an index page and an alphabetical list of pages. It assumes you know the component's name (e.g. 'Drive Couplings', 'Sprag'), so it is poor for someone who only knows what they need it to do. The 'Mechanisms' page is the exception: it lists mechanisms by the job they do
coverage.scope_match: medium: many in-scope TYPES are explained (flexible couplings, sprag/overrunning clutches, dog clutches, eddy-current clutches, ratchets and pawls, Geneva and other indexing mechanisms, escapements, harmonic, epicyclic and worm gears, differentials, screw-locking methods, snap-action/toggle mechanisms, and adhesive families by chemistry), but much of the site is standard-hardware dimension tables (screws, keys, circlips, pins, flanges, steel sections), which the project leaves out, and it has nothing on 3D printing, snap fits, compliant or print-in-place parts
coverage.taxonomy_used: Site-wide: by engineering subject area (about 36 resource sections on the Resources index, e.g. Adhesives, Circlips & Pins, Drive Components, Keyways, Machine Elements, Screws & Fastenings, Springs). The Mechanisms page uses a functional classification 'based on the type of motion required', taken from Uicker, Pennock and Shigley, with 17 groups: snap-action mechanisms, linear actuators, fine adjustment mechanisms, clamping mechanisms, location devices, ratchets, escapements, indexing mechanisms, swinging or rocking mechanisms, reciprocating mechanisms, reversing mechanisms, couplings and connectors, sliding connectors, stop/pause/hesitation mechanisms, curve generators, straight-line generators, tracing mechanisms. Locking devices are split into friction locking vs positive locking; clutches by how torque passes (friction, positive, magnetic, fluid); adhesives into natural, elastomer, thermoplastic, thermoset and toughened
coverage.example_types: sprag clutch (one-way / overrunning clutch); dog clutch (positive clutch); cone clutch; eddy-current clutch (magnetic clutch); fluid coupling (soft-start coupling); Bibby coupling (grid-spring coupling); spider / jaw coupling; beam coupling (helical-slot flexible coupling); diaphragm (disc) coupling; universal coupling (Hooke's / Cardan joint) and pin 'uni-joint'; pawl ratchet; spring-blade ratchet; magnetic (solenoid) ratchet; friction ratchet; Geneva mechanism (external, internal, spherical); mutilated gears (intermittent gearing); cycloidal intermittent gearing; harmonic drive (strain-wave gear); epicyclic (planetary) gears; differential gearbox; escapements; snap-action (toggle / bi-stable) mechanisms; Nyloc nut, castle nut with split pin, tab washer, wire locking, threadlocking (anaerobic) adhesive; adhesive families: PVA, cyanoacrylate (superglue), contact (rubber) adhesive, epoxy, anaerobic, acrylic solvent cement
coverage.making_methods: General mechanical engineering and machine design (industrial machinery, lifting equipment); nothing for 3D printing, laser cutting or hobby robotics
coverage.item_count: About 580 pages (roymech.org sitemap); 38 pages in Drive Components, 12 in Machine Elements, 10 in Springs, 18 in Screws, 4 main adhesive-type pages
coverage.special_behaviours_covered: One-way/ratchet: yes (sprag clutches for over-running, indexing or back-stopping; pawl, spring-blade, cam-driven, friction and magnetic ratchets). Indexing/detent: yes (Geneva, mutilated gears, cycloidal intermittent gearing; ratchet notes mention detents). Self-locking: partly (power screws pages; screw locking and retaining methods, friction vs positive locking) [uncertain]. Torque-limiting: not found as its own page (clutch and coupling pages only) [uncertain]. Over-centre: yes briefly, as snap-action toggle / bi-stable mechanisms. Hand-release only, compliant, print-in-place: no. Gear trains/gearboxes: yes, strong (spur, helical, bevel, worm, epicyclic, harmonic, differentials, gearbox thermal and efficiency). Powered connectors: partly (eddy-current and electromagnetic clutches, solenoid-driven magnetic ratchet, drive motors); no electromagnet or solenoid latches. Adhesives: yes, a generic-type guide covering natural, rubber/contact, thermoplastic (PVA, cyanoacrylate, acrylic solvent cement), thermoset (epoxy, phenolic), anaerobic and toughened adhesives, with which substrates each bonds, surface preparation and a shear/peel/temperature table
coverage.entry_structure: Page title, short definition, a table of types with one-paragraph descriptions and small GIF line drawings, sometimes formulae and dimension tables from British Standards, then a list of links to suppliers and further reading
coverage.audience_level: professional (design engineers and draughtsmen), also used by engineering students

usefulness.beginner_friendliness: medium: descriptions are short and practical, and type-comparison tables (couplings, clutches, adhesives) are easy to scan, but it uses engineering jargon without explanation, has typos, small dated diagrams and no animations
usefulness.has_images: yes: small, simple GIF line drawings on most component pages (couplings, indexing mechanisms, ratchets, locking devices); functional but low resolution and dated; some pages say pictures are at suppliers' sites instead
usefulness.has_animations: no animations, videos or interactive models on the pages opened
usefulness.gaps: No beginner layer or plain-English entry point; no function-based finder except the Mechanisms page; nothing on 3D printing, snap fits, print-in-place, compliant mechanisms, clever everyday connectors (cam buckles, cord locks, quick-release pins) or powered latches; no torque-limiter page; many outbound supplier links are old and likely dead [uncertain]; content largely frozen since 2009 on roymech.org; confusion between two domains
usefulness.good_for_entry_links: yes: stable, readable per-topic URLs that have kept the same paths since the 2000s, e.g. https://roymech.org/Useful_Tables/Drive/Clutches.html (sprag and dog clutches), https://roymech.org/Useful_Tables/Cams_Springs/Ratchets.html, https://roymech.org/Useful_Tables/Cams_Springs/Indexing.html. The same paths appear on roymech.co.uk in search results, so check which domain to use [uncertain]
usefulness.reusable_data: scrape-only: plain static HTML with an XML sitemap (https://roymech.org/sitemap.xml, 580 URLs); all rights reserved, so the list and text cannot be reused beyond linking and citing facts
usefulness.maintained: Split: roymech.org is a verbatim archive of the 2013-era content (footer (c) 2020, no new updates seen); roymech.co.uk is reported in search results as the official, actively maintained site restored by Andrew Wade, but could not be opened here [uncertain]. Wayback Machine could not be checked from this environment
usefulness.ideas_to_borrow: (1) One comparison table per family (type, how it works, notes, link), as on the Couplings and Clutches pages; ideal as the 'compare options' view at the end of a flow-chart branch. (2) The functional mechanism list (snap-action, clamping, location, ratchets, indexing, reversing, stop/pause ...) as flow-chart questions. (3) The friction-locking vs positive-locking split for anything that must not come loose. (4) The adhesive rule 'if two different materials are to be bonded, pick the adhesive that lists both' as a simple selector. (5) Stating when locking is really needed (guards, lifting, vibration, safety parts) before listing options
usefulness.design_rules_given: Yes, mostly for standard parts: adhesive shear strength (MPa), peel strength (N/mm) and temperature ranges by type; anaerobic retainers work with about 0.05 mm diametral clearance and an engagement length about 2x diameter; harmonic drives 30:1 to 350:1 per stage and usually below 6 kW; tapped-hole depth 1.5x diameter; key and spline strength, bolt preload and torque, spring design, ISO fits. Nothing for printed parts
usefulness.generator_or_parametric: No generators; formulae and tables only
usefulness.file_formats: HTML pages with GIF/JPG diagrams; links to external PDFs
usefulness.terminology_value: high for British/European engineering names and aliases (Bibby coupling, muff coupling, sprag clutch, mutilated gear, Nyloc/Simmonds nut, circlip, split cotter pin, tab washer) and for the matching BS/ISO/DIN standard numbers; no translations
usefulness.decision_support: Comparison tables for couplings, clutches, brakes and adhesives, plus the adhesive substrate-matching rule and the friction vs positive locking guidance; no interactive selector or flow chart
usefulness.derived_from_or_overlaps: Original notes by Roy Beardmore built on British Standards, suppliers' catalogues (Renold, Mayr, Warner etc.) and textbooks (the mechanism classification is credited to Uicker, Pennock and Shigley). roymech.org and roymech.co.uk carry the same original content, so count them once. Overlaps with engineeringtoolbox.com, Machinery's Handbook and Mecapedia for machine elements, and with Mechanisms and Mechanical Devices Sourcebook (Sclater) for ratchets and indexing mechanisms [uncertain]
